description: The metronome. Calibrated to measured serial architecture (serial-reference-A, 3,204 chapters) for a 1,337-chapter run. See engine/genre-priors.json and chapters/PLOT-ARCHITECTURE.md for what each number is answering.

chapter_target_words.note: Author's instruction: 5,000 words minimum. This is deliberately far above the measured serial median of 1,032 — 317 x 5,000 is a 1.6M-word novel with chapters five times the reference length. The measured architecture still applies to SHAPE (type transitions, payoff depth, self-contained openings); it no longer applies to LENGTH. Scene count per chapter should rise to 3-5 accordingly, or a 5,000-word chapter with one scene will sag.

beat_definitions.hook: Open a want or a threat the reader can name in one sentence.
beat_definitions.pressure: Force the POV character to spend something: time, trust, safety, or self-image.
beat_definitions.complication: The plan survives contact with the world, but deformed.
beat_definitions.cost: A loss that cannot be undone this arc. Never symmetrical with the gain.
beat_definitions.revelation: Recontextualize earlier material. Must cash a seed planted at least 3 chapters back.
beat_definitions.consolidation: The character metabolizes change. Lower tension, raise intimacy or dread.

tension_curve.note: Tension is 1-10. The engine computes a target per chapter; the author may deviate by 1 with a logged reason.

cadence_rules.note: Combat self-transitions at 50.2% and runs up to 23 chapters, so the action cap is a guard against drift, not a hard ceiling — a declared set-piece is exempt. Revelation is the connective tissue of the form (19.9% of chapters, most likely successor from nearly every mode), so its cadence is short.

introduction_budget.note: Two-tier cast. The persistent core keeps full dossier discipline; walk-ons are named, used and dropped, which is 33.6% of measured named entities.

payoff_window_chapters.note: Scaled to 317 chapters from the measured 40/120 at serial length.

seed_policy.note: Measured: a third of entity absences run 20+ chapters and still return, median long return 65, p90 475. The old 30-chapter rot threshold would have force-retired the form's deep plants.

progression_gates.note: Power/skill growth is rationed against chapter count so the MC never outruns the story.
progression_gates.cost_note: Every advance on a capability track must be paid for with a loss on a relational, moral, or physical track.

setback_policy.note: Raised to 0.30 for a tragedy. A protagonist on a fall must lose more often than a protagonist on a rise, or the fall reads as a power fantasy with a sad ending bolted on.

chapter_scenes.note: A chapter this long is a multi-scene unit. The measured 1-2 scene norm was for 1,000-word chapters.
